Permanent forest plots are a fundamental tool for monitoring how forests function and how they respond to global change. By re-measuring the same trees over time, they reveal changes in tree growth, mortality and recruitment, in species composition and in carbon storage. Yet such plots remain scarce on tropical islands, and especially in Melanesia. MELANOBS aims to help fill this gap.

The MELANOBS network is made up of permanent plots of 1 ha (100 m × 100 m). In each plot, every stem with a diameter at breast height (DBH, measured 1.3 m above the ground) of at least 10 cm is identified botanically, measured and mapped. This includes trees as well as palms, tree ferns, pandanus and other growth forms. Each individual carries a tag with a unique number, and the point of measurement is marked with paint so that every census measures the stem at exactly the same height.

The network focuses on lowland tropical wet forest. Plot locations are chosen together with local partners, preferably in protected and accessible areas. We are grateful to the customary landowners, local communities and protected-area managers who allow the plots to be established and monitored on their land.

A voucher specimen of each species recorded in the plots has been collected and deposited in the [herbaria](herbaria.qmd) of the region. For each species, both the scientific name and the local vernacular names are recorded, so that the data also document local knowledge of the flora.

Additional measurements are made in and around the plots, including tree height (H) and wood density. They are used to calibrate local height–diameter (H–DBH) allometries and to estimate above-ground biomass and carbon stocks.

The plots are resurveyed every year where possible, and at least every five years, to measure tree growth, mortality and recruitment rates, as well as changes in species composition. In addition, some trees are fitted with manual band dendrometers (EMS DB20) to measure their growth more accurately.

The protocol follows the international standards of the [ForestPlots.net](https://forestplots.net) network.

![The [Blue River Provincial Park](plots/blue-river.qmd) permanent plot. Left: canopy view showing the border of the plot and its 10 m × 10 m subplots. Right: mapped trees, with point size proportional to DBH and colour showing secondary growth rate between 2025 and 2026.](images/blue-river-figure.jpg){.wide-figure fig-alt="Left, a drone view of the forest canopy with the plot grid drawn on it; right, a map of the plot's trees as circles coloured by growth rate."}

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/map.R")
melanobs_map(show = "plots")
p <- read_plots()
knitr::kable(data.frame(paste0("[", p$site, "](plots/", p$slug, ".qmd)"),
                        p$island, p$country, coord(p$lat), coord(p$lon)),
             col.names = c("Plot", "Island", "Country", "Latitude", "Longitude"))
```
